title: Why Is DraftKings Stock Crashing, and is it a Buying Opportunity? | DKNG Stock Near 52 Week Low
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc asks whether DraftKings' crash to near its 52-week low is a buying opportunity. He argues the story has flipped: prediction markets went from a regulatory headwind to a growth driver, with 1M+ customers on the prediction-market product and millions expected by end of NFL season, so DraftKings wins in either regulatory outcome. Management is pulling planned 2027 marketing spend into 2026 because customer acquisition economics are unusually lucrative relative to long-term customer value — but investors hated the spend and punished the stock. Valuation: forward P/E of just 11 near the $18.52 52-week low ($18.59 at analysis), the cheapest it's ever been, implying expectations of flat to low-single-digit growth; his DCF agrees the stock looks attractive. However, he stresses competition is fiercer than ever and DraftKings must adapt in unfamiliar ways, so he raised the beta in his DCF to reflect higher forward risk — and it still screens cheap. Verdict: DKNG — CONDITIONAL_BUY @ $18.59, for high-risk-tolerance investors only; his first call on the name. Bull: prediction-market customer growth restores the growth trajectory. Bear: intense competition, front-loaded marketing spend, regulatory uncertainty.
